assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction overcame a limit on electron lenses that had stood since Scherzer's 1936 theorem, and delivered sub-angstrom resolution in transmission and scanning transmission electron microscopy. This is a clear invention with a clear discovery content: atomic-scale imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects and functional materials in physics, chemistry and materials science, now routine worldwide. The impact is lasting and demonstrated in thousands of results, and the invention is crisp enough for the 'discovery or invention' criterion. I note that this is my own field, so I weigh it against a field-neutral standard.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider led the construction and first working implementation in TEM, and Urban led the Julich effort that showed the atomic-resolution gain. The credited trio is a coherent and fair configuration. Other groups, notably the STEM corrector development outside this list, also made decisive contributions and are not among the credited names, so the allocation is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Correctors have been commercial for over two decades, resolution gains are independently confirmed in many laboratories, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: The credited names omit the independent STEM aberration-corrector line of work, which could force a different allocation of credit or a larger conflict over priority.
Whether the committee prefers to honour an enabling instrument over a discovery of nature is a matter of judgment, not evidence.
I have not independently verified the exact dates and roles of each credited person.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicted flat bands at a magic twist angle, and experiment then found correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene. This opened moire quantum matter as a tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological phases, with very rapid and broad impact in condensed matter physics. The discovery is original, clear and has generated a large new field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive 2011 prediction of the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states. Theory and experiment are cleanly split across the credited trio. Other contributors, such as the Dean group with hBN and other twisted-bilayer experiments, are not credited, and the supplied credit cannot settle their roles.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature. The key phenomena have been reproduced by many groups, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the origin of the correlated states are unsettled.
Recognition may be early relative to the field's eventual settled picture.
Contributions of other experimental groups and the role of high-quality hBN substrates are not resolved in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength trapping idea with large ensembles of neutral atoms, reaching fractional uncertainties in the 10^-18 range and enabling tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear invention with a clearly measurable performance record.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first realisations; Ye brought the clock to record accuracy and stability and developed the strontium systems and many-body aspects. Two names make a clean and fair allocation. Prior prizes to Hall, Haensch and Wineland cover combs and ion clocks but not this specific invention.
assessment.maturity: Mature in performance terms and independently confirmed in several laboratories. The redefinition of the second has not yet happened, which is a timing consideration but not a scientific doubt.
uncertainties: The committee may judge the incremental step beyond optical frequency combs and ion clocks to be too small.
Contributions from other groups on ytterbium and ion clocks are not part of the credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO barriers, with coherent spin-dependent tunnelling predicted by theory and realised experimentally, raised room-temperature magnetoresistance from tens to hundreds of percent. This made it the basis of modern read heads and magnetic random-access memory. The physics of symmetry-filtered tunnelling is a clean, quantitative example linking electronic structure at an oxide interface to a device effect. I find interface structure particularly persuasive here.
assessment.attribution: Butler and collaborators made the theoretical prediction, and Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated large effects in 2004. The three-person credit is plausible, but the experimental priority between the two groups, and the earlier contributions on amorphous barriers, are not resolved by the supplied credit. Part of the credit could instead be considered covered by the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance.
assessment.maturity: Mature, since the effect is widely reproduced and commercially deployed. It is not premature.
uncertainties: The relation to the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize could make the committee see it as a refinement.
Other theorists who proposed coherent tunnelling in the same period are not credited.
Whether device engineering or fundamental physics dominates the contribution is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator were a conceptual advance in condensed matter: a new topological classification of band insulators with protected edge states, followed by experimental realisation. The idea is original, clear and has driven a large body of work on topological materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical proposal and Z2 classification, and Molenkamp's group gave the decisive experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells. The credited names do not include the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction for HgTe or the three-dimensional topological insulator work, so the credit is incomplete and arguably contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature in concept and experiment, and independently confirmed. Practical applications are still limited, but the Nobel criterion does not require them.
uncertainties: The priority between predictions for HgTe quantum wells and the three-dimensional generalisation is not resolved here.
This candidate overlaps with B038, and a prize should not split the same discovery.
Applications and the robustness of edge transport remain incompletely demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the later association with a blazar and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy at energies far beyond earlier detectors. The detector is a large invention built in Antarctic ice, and the discovery is clear and scientifically important.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the scientific driver of the IceCube concept, and Karle and Spiering held key leadership and physics roles in a collaboration of hundreds of people. The 'three-person limit' fits poorly with a large collaboration, and the supplied credit cannot show who was decisive.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature as a discovery, since the diffuse flux has been confirmed with several analyses. Source identification remains incomplete.
uncertainties: The allocation of credit in a very large collaboration is unresolved.
Source associations are still developing and may later reshape the story.
Earlier detectors such as AMANDA also contributed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultrapure hexagonal boron nitride crystals, with very low defect densities, became the standard encapsulating and dielectric layer for graphene and other two-dimensional materials. They enabled high-mobility devices, the fractional quantum Hall effect in graphene and much of the moire physics. The enabling role in new physics is large, though the contribution is materials growth rather than a discovery of a phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: Taniguchi and Watanabe developed the high-pressure growth of the crystals and supplied them to most groups. Kim's group demonstrated key device uses, but so did other groups, notably Dean and Hone, so I omit Kim for now. The proposed two-person credit is plausible but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Mature in use, since the material is used worldwide. Recognition could be considered either timely or as part of a larger 2D materials prize.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether a materials-growth contribution meets the 'discovery or invention' standard.
The relative role of device groups is not resolved by the supplied credit.
It could be better recognised together with a moire or 2D-materials prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Rydberg blockade provides strong, controllable interactions between neutral atoms, and programmable atom arrays now serve for quantum simulation and gate-based quantum computing. The idea is original and the platform has produced striking experiments with tens to hundreds of atoms.
assessment.attribution: Lukin and collaborators proposed the Rydberg-blockade ideas with theorists, Saffman contributed gate proposals and demonstrations, and Browaeys demonstrated blockade with single atoms. Contributions of the theory proposal by Jaksch, Cirac, Zoller and others, and of Weiss, Lukin's collaborators and others, are not in the credited set, so the allocation is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Still maturing. Error rates and scaling are improving rapidly, and the long-term picture of what this platform achieves is not settled.
uncertainties: Recognition may be premature.
The theory-to-experiment credit chain is complex and not fully captured by the supplied names.
Overlap with other atomic quantum-information candidates in the longlist is not resolved.
